title: Invalid G7 start time sent to AAPS
body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/discussions/3249
Originally posted by **jgslade** December 21, 2023 The Classic Status Page is showing the start date of my previous sensor but the G5/G6/G7 status page and the home screen are showing the correct sensor age. ![image](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/assets/29897815/4e3be447-e37f-4c3e-b756-2a80dc44eb05) ![image](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/assets/29897815/713bf680-d20f-42a6-8b51-9cc781a3bb9e) ![image](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/assets/29897815/38ebcc52-03bc-418e-b39c-74afed068881)

comments.body: So I believe that the cause of this would be if xDrip doesn't register the sensor stopping for your previous sensor session. Do you think that could have happened? I think that when xDrip gets the last reading from your old sensor it will mark the sensor session as stopped and that will reset that timer. We might be able to put some failsafes in for this but I'm wondering if you can share whether you think that could be what happened here?

@jamorham 
I am looking at my classic status page and see the start time is shown to have been on November 27, almost a month ago.
But, I switched to a new device 5 days ago.

I waited for my previous device to stop working.  But, I never tapped on stop sensor and I don't want to do that even if it is still running.  
At that point, I changed the transmitter ID.

@jamorham that is likely I often don't wait till the very end of the sensor
to switch to the new one. I presoak the new one for a few hours and then
switch when it's most convenient for me.

My sensor just reached 10.5 days and stopped working.
The status page showed sensor expired, not stopped.
The classic status page still showed a few days ago when I installed xDrip last.

I then changed the transmitter ID to that of the new device that had been running for 12 hours.
xDrip has connected to the new device and is showing readings from the new device.
The classic status page still shows the time from a few days ago when I reinstalled xDrip.

xDrip shows 3 start times for G6.  

1- Transmitter activation time on G5/G6/G7 status page as "Transmitter Days" reported by the transmitter
2- Session start time on G5/G6/G7 status page as "Sensor Status" reported by transmitter
3- xDrip sensor start time on Classic status page as "Sensor Start" maintained by xDrip and not coming from the transmitter

2 and 3 are not necessarily the same for G6 for example if you start the sensor with your receiver or a t:slim pump.
There have been requests to make the two match.  I'd rather we remove something than to make it redundant.  But, let's not talk about G6 anymore.

When you use a G7, there is only one start time and that is the moment you use the applicator to insert the device.

We don't reinvent the wheel every time a new device is added to xDrip.  We use the existing code as much as possible and we gradually tweak it to cleanup any discrepancies for the new device.
We have already made changes to xDrip to make G7 notes more relevant and valid.  There are more open PRs that continue in that path that are waiting to be reviewed and hopefully merged soon.

Let's see what's the best way to update the classic status page with respect to the sensor start time.

In my opinion, there is no value in maintaining the time xDrip first becomes aware of a new G7 device.  There is no way we can use a G7 in non-native mode.  So, I suggest we remove sensor start from the classic status page.

This brings me  to my question, how this relate to AAPS.

Which build option should I use? For AAPS I use the generate signed Bundle/APK, do I do the same thing with xDrip?

That's what I do.  But, please note that you will not be able to install it over the official release.  You will either need to use a test phone, or uninstall before installing.  If you uninstall, you will lose all your xDrip history and settings.  So, please plan this carefully.

Can I save the settings to a settings file then load from the settings file?

It looks like it successfully built.

If you are currently using the official xDrip, you can create a backup on Google Drive.  it backs up both database and settings.  https://navid200.github.io/xDrip/docs/GoogleDriveBackup.html

After you are done with the test, you can install the official release again and restore the backup.

If you want your settings for the test, save the settings in a file and you will be able to restore after installing your version.
https://navid200.github.io/xDrip/docs/CopySettings.html
